en: Vulcan Point is a tiny island inside Taal Lake that is actually a volcano situated within a larger volcano.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River flows directly into the sea, meaning its water levels change with the ocean tides.
Mount Hamiguitan in Davao Oriental features a unique pygmy forest where century-old bonsai trees grow only a meter tall.
The famous Chocolate Hills of Bohol consist of exactly 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped limestone mounds covered in green grass.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous worldwide for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cones on Earth.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro holds the highest concentration of shorefish biodiversity in the entire world.
The island province of Camiguin has seven volcanoes, which is more volcanoes than the number of its municipalities.
The Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park protects the critically endangered Philippine crocodile, the rarest crocodilian in the world.
The Pearl of Puerto Princesa, found in Palawan, is one of the largest natural pearls ever discovered globally.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is the only Philippine region composed entirely of landlocked provinces that do not touch the ocean.
Davao City in Mindanao is the largest city in the Philippines by land area, covering over 2,400 square kilometers.
The island of Mindoro is the exclusive natural habitat of the tamaraw, a small dwarf buffalo found nowhere else.
